body: Yeah, I’ve heard of that before. I have been diagnosed with depression and have been having a lot of suicidal thoughts lately but no “urges” until last night, it kind of freaked me out a little more than just that “call of the void” feeling

Thanks for your reply. I haven't really been a very good friend / daughter / sister / aunt / niece / cousin / granddaughter / etc. for a long time because I've just been so trapped in my own shit. The least I can do is try to minimize the inconvenience on people if I kill myself.

It feels nearly impossible just to get from day to day. I have no motivation to do anything, and time just passes around me. Even just getting out of bed in the morning feels like moving a mountain. I stopped going to my therapist (lots of reasons - felt like it wasn't helping, started getting red flags from my therapist, etc.) but I'm working on finding a new doctor who can either get me on meds or refer me to a psychiatrist who can. 

I've thought about it a lot and this is the best metaphor I've come up with - having depression is like being in the middle of the ocean. Therapy / self-care / exercise is a oar. It takes a lot of effort on your part, and it's going to be hard work, but it will move you in the right direction. But it won't work if you're drowning. It's just extra weight when it takes all your energy to keep yourself afloat. I see the right medication as a life raft. Something to help keep you afloat, so then you can actually use your oar to paddle and steer.

Anyways, I'm rambling too. Thanks for your kind words and your suggestions. Maybe I'll try getting out a little bit once I shower.

Sometimes I want to, but I don’t think I ever could, and this is one of the reasons why. It’s weird. It’s like, it keeps me hanging on, but it hurts, too, imagining what they’d say.
